title: Puff stitch rectangle wrap
subtitle: Alternating 5-loop puff stitches and chain spaces in aran weight on a 5 mm hook, 170 cm x 55 cm
excerpt: A five-loop puff stitch creates a rounded, bobble-like cluster by drawing up five loops in the same stitch before closing them together. Set against chain spaces, the puffs sit in a regular grid that gives the fabric both texture and drape. This rectangle wrap uses aran weight yarn on a 5 mm hook and measures 170 cm wide by 55 cm deep.
sourceNotes: Puff stitch rectangle construction synthesised for Homemade. The five-loop puff stitch worked in alternating rows with chain-1 spaces is a standard fibre arts technique with no single original source.
heroPrompt: A chunky crochet wrap in warm terracotta aran yarn folded over a wooden stool. The rows of raised puff stitches and the chain-space grid are clearly visible in directional light.

glossaryTerms.definition: A cluster stitch made by drawing up multiple loops in the same stitch before closing them all at once with a final yarn-over-draw-through. In this pattern a 5-loop puff: (yarn over, insert hook in stitch, draw up a loop) 5 times -- 11 loops on hook -- yarn over, draw through all 11 loops. Ch 1 to close.
A row where puff stitches alternate with ch-1 spaces. The puffs sit in the ch-1 spaces of the previous puff row, staggering the grid on alternate rows.

content.text: This rectangular wrap is worked flat in rows, using an alternating pattern of
puff stitches

and chain spaces on every right-side row, with double crochet rows on every wrong-side row. Each puff uses five loops drawn up in the same space. The ch-1 that closes each puff counts as the chain space for the following row, so the puffs on alternate rows sit directly above the chain spaces of the previous puff row.

Aran weight yarn on a 5 mm hook produces substantial, warm fabric. The puff stitch draws in more yarn than a plain row, so tension matters: measure your gauge swatch across the full 10-repeat width before committing to the cast-on count. The stated foundation chain of 172 stitches gives 85 puff positions per puff row at gauge.

attrs.title: Materials
attrs.body: Approximately 600 g aran-weight yarn (a smooth, lightly twisted yarn shows the puff shapes most clearly). A 5 mm hook (US H/8). Tapestry needle. Craft scissors. Stitch markers. Blocking mat and pins. Tape measure.

content.text: Gauge

1 puff stitch + 1 ch-1 space = 2 cm wide; 1 puff row + 1 plain row = 2 cm tall. Over 10 puff repeats the work measures 20 cm wide. Work a swatch of at least 12 puff repeats across and 10 rows tall in the full puff-and-plain pattern, block it, and measure the central 10-repeat width and 5-row height.
Stitches used
ch: chain -- UK and US shared.
sl st: slip stitch -- UK and US shared.
dc: double crochet (UK) -- worked on every plain row. The same move as US single crochet (sc).
Puff stitch
: (yarn over, insert hook in ch-1 space, draw up a loop to 1 cm height) 5 times -- 11 loops on hook -- yarn over, draw through all 11 loops. Ch 1 to secure.
Pattern

The wrap is worked from one short end to the other (the 55 cm measurement builds up over rows). The long measurement (170 cm) is the foundation chain width. The ch-1 turning chain does not count as a stitch in this pattern.
Foundation chain
Ch 172. (170 working stitches plus 2 for the first row's turning chain.)
Row 1 (wrong side, plain row)
Ch 1 (does not count as a stitch). 1 dc in 2nd ch from hook. 1 dc in each ch across. Turn. (170 sts)
Row 2 (right side, puff row)
Ch 1 (does not count as a stitch). 1 dc in first st. Ch 1. *1
puff stitch
in next st. Ch 1. Skip 1 st.* Repeat from * to * to last st. 1 dc in last st. Turn. (85 puffs, 2 edge dc)
Row 3 (wrong side, plain row)
Ch 1 (does not count as a stitch). 1 dc in first st (edge dc from previous row). 1 dc in each ch-1 space and each puff stitch across, ending 1 dc in final edge dc. Turn. (170 sts)
Row 4 (right side, staggered puff row)
Ch 1 (does not count as a stitch). 1 dc in first st. *Skip 1 st. Ch 1. 1
puff stitch
in next st.* Repeat from * to * to last 2 sts. Ch 1. 1 dc in last st. Turn. (85 puffs, 2 edge dc)
Rows 5 to 55 -- full repeat
Rows 1 to 4 form the basic
puff row
repeat. Continue alternating puff rows (rows 2 and 4) with plain dc rows (row 3 pattern) until the work measures 55 cm from the foundation chain. End with a completed plain dc row. Fasten off.
Finishing

Weave in all ends securely on the wrong side. Wet-block by soaking in cool water for 10 minutes, pressing excess water out in a towel without wringing, then pinning to the stated dimensions on a blocking mat. Puff stitch fabric relaxes slightly when blocked; pin the short ends first to set the width, then ease the long edges into position.
Care
Handwash in cool water with a gentle wool or fibre wash. Do not tumble-dry. Lay flat on a clean towel, ease to shape, and leave to dry. Re-block if the puff texture flattens after washing.
What to try next

A 3-loop puff in DK weight on a 4 mm hook produces a finer, lighter fabric from the same construction. Replacing the plain dc rows with a row of ch-1 spaces between puffs opens the fabric into a more lacy structure. Working two colours in alternating puff rows creates a striped texture where the colour contrast emphasises the raised puff grid.
